summary: The primary objective of our innovative engineering project was to safely and efficiently remove defunct satellites and hazardous orbital space debris from Earth's increasingly crowded orbit by utilizing high-powered superconducting magnets configured with identical magnetic poles to gently push them out of their existing trajectories and into deep space; this contactless magnetic repulsion approach not only significantly reduced overall mission and operational costs, but also completely eliminated the need for extra chemical propellant and substantially minimized the number of potentially problematic mechanical stages throughout the entire deorbiting process.
details: 1. What Is Its Primary Objective? Thousands of defunct satellites, having completed their operational lifespans, drift through Low Earth Orbit (LEO) at speeds of approximately $28,000\text{ km/h}$. This situation poses risks such as the fragmentation of active satellites, potential loss of human life among astronauts, and the onset of the "Kessler Syndrome"—a scenario that could effectively bring the space age to an end. The primary objectives of the AUTS (Active Unused Satellite System) are: to safely remove large, hazardous, defunct satellites from orbit; to propel them—not into Earth's atmosphere (where they might damage the ozone layer, leave behind metallic dust, or pose a risk of falling to the surface)—but rather into deep space, in a direction opposite to the Solar System's motion; and to remain in orbit for repeated use, rather than self-destructing after a single mission. 2. How Does It Work? (Operational Logic, Step-by-Step) Safe Staging (Parking Orbit and Sleep Mode): When not engaged in an active mission, the AUTS remains in a "parking orbit"—a region with minimal collision risk—operating in an energy-saving "sleep mode." It is activated upon receiving the coordinates of a target satellite from a ground station or an AI-driven tracking system. Intersecting and Tangential Approach: The AUTS approaches the target satellite not head-on, but at an oblique (tangential) angle. This maneuver allows the system to leverage the satellite's existing orbital velocity to its own advantage. Non-Contact Magnetic Propulsion ("Kinetic Billiards"): When the two objects reach their closest point of tangential proximity, 25-Tesla REBCO superconducting magnets—integrated into both the AUTS and a new generation of satellites designed for future launch—are activated. Without the use of any physical hooks, nets, or capture arms, an inert satellite is deflected from its orbit through the application of a powerful magnetic repulsive force. Ejection into Deep Space: By leveraging this acquired angular momentum, the inert satellite escapes Earth's gravitational pull—without the need for an additional booster rocket—and is propelled into deep space, moving in the direction opposite to the Solar System's motion, thereby leaving Earth behind forever. Recoil Control (Stabilization): To prevent the AUTS (Active Uncooperative Target System) from spinning or drifting uncontrollably in space—as dictated by Newton's Third Law of Motion (Action-Reaction)—telescopic shock-absorption systems integrated into the craft's chassis are deployed, alongside low-propellant Argon/Krypton ion thrusters.1.
